sources.title: Problem Solving 5 — Magnetic Force, Torque, and Magnetic Moments
sources.authority: Massachusetts Institute of Technology — MIT OpenCourseWare

version.rule: Exact MIT OCW course/resource identity and published Spring 2005 problem-solving PDF.

rights.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; MIT OCW explicitly permits AI training/use subject to its licence restrictions

evidence.basis: MIT OCW states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and explicitly permits AI training/use when attribution, non-commercial and ShareAlike requirements are met.
The official resource page identifies the exact 259 kB PDF, course, level and physics problem-solving objectives.

sources.benchmarkFocus: Dense electromagnetism reasoning with diagrams, derivation steps and multiple linked questions.

The official copyright page identifies the PSF License Version 2 and the additional 0BSD treatment for documentation code examples.

sources.title: Declaration of Independence (1776) — National Archives transcript
sources.authority: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration

version.rule: Official NARA transcript of the Stone Engraving, with exact web bytes additionally bound by SHA-256.

rights.license: U.S. Government/NARA-produced web content public domain; NARA states worldwide reuse under CC0 1.0

evidence.basis: NARA states that works it produces are public domain and available worldwide under CC0 1.0; it asks users to credit NARA as source.
The official National Archives page provides the historical document context and transcript used by this benchmark.

sources.benchmarkFocus: Primary historical source: tests attribution, context and the distinction between source claims and neutral historical synthesis.

sources.title: Règlement (UE) 2016/679 — RGPD, texte du Journal officiel en français
sources.authority: Office des publications de l’Union européenne — EUR-Lex

version.rule: Exact CELEX identifier and Official Journal publication state, not a silently updated consolidated text.

rights.license: EU legal-document reuse policy under Decision 2011/833/EU; commercial and non-commercial reuse unless otherwise specified

evidence.basis: EUR-Lex states that, unless otherwise specified, legal documents may be reused for commercial or non-commercial purposes.
The official EUR-Lex record binds the regulation to CELEX 32016R0679 and the 4 May 2016 Official Journal version.

sources.benchmarkFocus: Normative legal text: tests article/recital distinction and fidelity to one exact official version.

sources.title: Flash sécurité patient — Retranscription des prescriptions médicamenteuses

version.rule: Publication date of the selected HAS safety resource.

rights.license: French public-information reuse regime for HAS-owned public information

evidence.basis: HAS states that public information for which it owns the rights may be reused subject to source/date attribution and non-alteration, while third-party content is excluded.

sources.benchmarkFocus: Patient-safety content where a plausible simplification can become semantically unsafe if the document status or caution is distorted.

sources.title: Molière — Le Tartuffe ou L’Imposteur, édition Jean Ribou 1669 — texte brut Gallica

version.rule: Exact Gallica ARK and historical edition; OCR/text bytes are additionally bound by SHA-256.

rights.license: BnF/Gallica reuse conditions for digitized public-domain collections; commercial reuse may require separate conditions

evidence.basis: BnF distinguishes metadata and digitized-document reuse; the benchmark remains in the declared non-commercial R&D context.
The stable Gallica ARK identifies the exact historical edition used for the benchmark.
BnF documents the .texteBrut API for retrieving full text from an exact Gallica ARK and notes API rate limits.

sources.benchmarkFocus: Historical OCR/edition fidelity: the kit must stay bound to one exact edition and surface uncertainty rather than silently normalize it.
